Right now they each tell their own story. Your job is to make them tell one. We are looking for a Systems Engineer to connect sensors like aerostats, radars, and cameras into the Navy's communications systems. All that information comes together in an operational picture, the single map that Navy watch teams use to see what is happening at sea. You help make that map complete and trustworthy. Partner navies should be able to work side by side with US forces, and also handle things on their own. What you build gets used, not filed away. Day to day, that looks like: Connecting sensors, networks, and software so they talk to each other Working across the whole build: planning it, designing it, coding it, testing it, and keeping it running Turning what the customer needs into clear technical requirements Helping test the system, then fixing what testing turns up Working with Navy staff, program leads, and other companies on the team Good systems engineers keep one eye on the big picture and one on the details. You will think about cost and schedule too, not just the technology. What we are looking for At least 3 years of related systems engineering experience A good grasp of systems engineering basics: figuring out requirements, designing the approach, putting the pieces together, and proving it works Hands-on experience connecting different networks, software, and hardware Bachelor's degree (required) Active Secret clearance (required) that you can maintain. The specific equipment is learnable. Knowing how to make systems fit together is the part that matters. Why you might like it here Your work shows up on a screen someone uses to make a real call. We are a small team, so you own your piece from start to finish instead of inheriting a slice of someone else's design. And it is four days on-site, not five.
